title.narrative: Integrated and sustainable management of natural resources in the lowerMekong contributes to the sustainable development in the subregion.

description.narrative: Aims at promoting healthy riverine environment to support ecosystem services, including fish migration and reproduction, and maintaining water quality for the protection of human health; aquatic life and agriculture. This will contribute to reduced poverty among vulnerable people dependent on river and wetland resources. The activity supports the achievement of outcome 1.1 of the Basin Development Strategy 20212030 (Adequate water flow and quality for a healthy environment and productive communities), and outcome 2.2 (Increased employment and reduced poverty among vulnerable people dependent on river and wetland resources).

title.narrative: Outcome 5. Effective dialogue and cooperation between Member Countries and strategic engagement of regional partners and stakeholders on transboundary water management

description.narrative: The intent of this Outcome is to enhance close collaboration with the MRCs Dialogue Partners China and Myanmar who are critically important in the overall management of the river as the riparian of the Upper Mekong. It also places emphasis on the engagement with other partners and stakeholders a distinctive mark of Mekong cooperation through the MRC in an open, inclusive and transparent manner. To achieve the outcome, the MRC uplifts the partnership with the Dialogue Partners through joint activities and events with the Dialogue Partners and other regional frameworks. Engagement with stakeholder is expanded through regional and national consultations. Partnership with CSOs is strengthened through their participations in the MRC events and contributions in key strategic plans.

description.narrative: This activity aims to strengthen and transform the MRC Secretariat to a leaner and more transparent, accountable, and costeffective organization, funded by the Member Countries, as a direct result of reforms in human resources, administration, and finance systems. This will be achieved through the improvement of the Financial Management Information System, organizational capacity, and procedural mechanisms, production of more relevant, valueadded and important outputs for regional and national water resources development and management, and sharpening of its core functions to avoid duplication and complements other broader cooperation mechanisms towards common basin and regional objectives.

description.narrative: This outcome targets the contribution of the five MRC Procedures in avoiding, minimizing and mitigating potential adverse transboundary impacts from development activities along the Mekong mainstream and its tributaries. The five MRC Procedures PDIES, PWUM, PMFM, PWQ and PNPCA represent the most comprehensive set for water management on an international river in the developing world. To achieve the outcome, the MRC implements and enhances its procedures through Joint Committee Statement and Joint Action Plan, comprehensive technical proposal, update guidelines for PNPCA and PDIES, and monitoring of environmental impacts from hydropower projects.
